source.interpretation: The limits file contains planning/experiment budgets; listing a value here is not evidence that it was measured or achieved.

dataAndServiceBoundary.fixtureData: Synthetic workspace IDs, entity IDs, revisions, sequences, encrypted-manifest byte shapes, attachment references, object-version identities, usage-ledger rows, device leases, snapshots, and recovery metadata only.
dataAndServiceBoundary.futureDatabaseHarness: Any later behavior run requires a disposable isolated PostgreSQL database/schema with synthetic rows and no production credentials; none was provisioned or contacted for this plan.
dataAndServiceBoundary.futureObjectStoreHarness: Any later provider behavior run requires a disposable isolated versioned object-store bucket containing synthetic objects; no provider, bucket, endpoint, or service was contacted for this plan.

fixtures.setup: Use synthetic live entities and immutable manifest DTOs in a disposable workspace; introduce a concurrent entity write while the snapshot worker is waiting to acquire the workspace lock.
fixtures.action: Plan a bounded READ COMMITTED materialization transaction that takes the workspace lock first, reads epoch and high-water H after the lock, inserts snapshot rows and attachment refs, then persists rowCount and ready state.
assertions: The snapshot records the epoch and H read after acquiring the workspace lock, and its rows represent that fixed state.
snapshot_rows and snapshot_attachment_refs become visible with the ready snapshot in the same transaction; a failed materialization does not publish a partial ready snapshot.
The materialization transaction is bounded, does not retain a transaction handle for later pages, and performs no S3 or other network call while holding the workspace lock.

fixtures.setup: A synthetic ready snapshot contains multiple entity IDs; additional synthetic creates, updates, and deletes occur after H while the client requests multiple pages.
fixtures.action: Plan page reads with the same snapshotId, epoch, and H using an entityId keyset, then plan catchup from H with a fixed upper sequence.
assertions: Every page comes from the same materialized snapshot and does not fall through to current heads or OFFSET pagination.
Writes with seq greater than H appear in catchup rather than changing already materialized snapshot rows.
Page requests do not keep a database connection or lock open across requests; drafts remain separate until validation and atomic namespace swap.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic active device leases, a valid ready snapshot at H, change-log entries above H, and immutable versions/attachments are arranged around the permitted GC prefix.
fixtures.action: Plan log/version/attachment GC while paging and catchup remain outstanding; repeat after snapshot expiry and after a lease becomes expired.
assertions: A valid snapshot pins its attachment refs and all catchup change-log entries with seq greater than H and their corresponding versions until expiry.
The safe log-GC prefix does not pass the minimum of active lease appliedSeq values and valid ready snapshot H values; when the protected set is empty, the specified bound is lastSeq.
An expired device is moved to snapshot_required and no longer blocks GC through its stale appliedSeq; changing only a sequence number cannot restore it to active.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic snapshot requests cover building, ready, expired, and epoch-changed states; page requests are attempted before ready and after expiry/epoch change.
fixtures.action: Plan page access and client restart decisions for each lifecycle state.
assertions: Snapshot pages are unavailable before ready.
An expired snapshot maps to the specified SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED result and an epoch change maps to EPOCH_MISMATCH; the client starts a new snapshot rather than continuing the old page stream.
The fixture asserts no other snapshot failure code or retry mapping until that mapping is frozen.

fixtures.setup: Prepare synthetic workspaces at the configured 50,000 live-entity limit, including history, saved, collection, and collection_entry entities; create a separate injected 50,001-row over-limit fixture. Include a manifest payload at the configured 16,384-byte inline boundary and record its snapshot DTO size separately.
fixtures.action: Plan pre-count, bounded snapshot materialization, and the experiment against snapshotStatementTimeoutMs without increasing configured limits.
assertions: The snapshot row count includes live history, saved, collection, and collection_entry entities; retired tombstones and old versions do not count as snapshot rows.

The 50,000-row maximum fixture is measured against the 2,000 ms snapshot statement budget; if the limit cannot be met, the specified response is to stop new workspace cloud writes or optimize materialization, not to remove the lock or use unbounded selection.
The 50,001-row injected over-limit fixture is counted and rejected before unbounded materialization; its exact external error/job mapping remains OPEN_QUESTION.
The configured 16,384-byte inline manifest boundary and the serialized snapshot-row DTO are recorded as separate quantities until their exact size-accounting relationship is specified.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic device state is placed just before and at the configured 90-day offline lease expiry. In the reused-snapshot branch, priorSeenHighWater=120 and valid reused snapshot H=90 for the same epoch; appliedSeq is lower than server high-water.
fixtures.action: Plan expiry handling, reuse/download of snapshot H=90, fixed-H catchup through seq 120, and bootstrap acknowledgement tied to that snapshot; keep the old namespace active until catchup validation completes.
assertions: An expired device enters snapshot_required; an ordinary ACK or a manually increased appliedSeq cannot activate it or extend its lease.

An authorized device can reactivate only after validating every snapshot page and catchup through at least H, then submitting a bootstrap ACK tied to the snapshot; the server validates snapshot ownership, epoch, H, and the ACK floor before marking active and establishing a new lease.
Unsent drafts and old outbox state remain separate from the recovery namespace until validation and atomic swap; a stale outbox is not blindly replayed.

For the explicit priorSeenHighWater=120 and reused snapshot H=90 branch, the old namespace remains published and no swap occurs at H=90; swap is allowed only after catchup reaches at least seq 120 and the recovery namespace validates.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic versions and an attachment are referenced by combinations of current heads, valid change_log rows, retained old versions, trash heads, saved items, and snapshot pins.
fixtures.action: Plan candidate selection and reference recheck immediately before GC marks an attachment deleting.
assertions: The protected reference set includes current versions, still-valid change_log references, retained old versions, recycle-bin/trash references, and valid snapshot pins.
A current head is never removed by version TTL, and a shared blob remains protected while any saved item, retained version, trash head, log, or snapshot references it.
Only versions whose reference and retention conditions have all cleared become GC candidates; the fixture does not invent an unreferenced-version selection order.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic entity versions include an old current head, a deleted head older than versionHistoryDays, and a shared blob still referenced by a saved item.
fixtures.action: Plan history expiry, deletion into trash, trash TTL expiry, and reference-aware GC at the configured 30-day boundaries.
assertions: History/version expiry does not remove a current head, and deleting an entity moves its last head to trash_head_version_id with trash_expires_at equal to deleted_at plus trashDays.
A head older than versionHistoryDays remains protected through trashDays; after trash expiry, any remaining log, retained-version, saved-item, or snapshot reference still prevents deletion.
Removing a collection relationship does not delete its saved target, and a later repin uses a new relationship ID.

fixtures.setup: Use synthetic counts liveEntities=49,999 and retiredIds=950,000 (sum 999,999 of maxRetiredIdsPerWorkspace=1,000,000), with maxLiveEntitiesPerWorkspace=50,000; one create can reserve the final retirement slot.
fixtures.action: Plan one create that reserves the last slot, deletion of a different live entity converting its already-reserved slot to retired, a subsequent extra create attempt at the full lifetime budget, and replay/recreation of a retired ID.
assertions: Maintain liveEntities <= maxLiveEntitiesPerWorkspace and liveEntities + retiredIds <= maxRetiredIdsPerWorkspace; a create is admitted only when liveEntities + retiredIds + 1 <= maxRetiredIdsPerWorkspace and the live cap also permits it.

The in-budget create reserves one future retirement slot. Deleting a live entity decreases liveEntities and converts its already-reserved slot into retiredIds, so the sum stays constant; deletion does not request a new slot and is never refused because the fence is full.

At the full lifetime ID budget, further create is blocked and the export or explicit new-workspace migration entry point is offered; fences are not compacted/deleted and history clearing does not reset identity.
Live and retired counts remain separately tracked under the single combined lifetime-ID budget; retired IDs and old versions are not snapshot rows.
A retired entity ID is never reused.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic ready attachment has zero references; include one remaining physical object version, a concurrent attempted new reference, and variants where provider deletion fails or only a delete marker is returned.
fixtures.action: Plan GC state transition, business outbox write, out-of-transaction physical-version deletion, confirmation, and ledger reconciliation.
assertions: GC follows workspace then ledger then attachment lock order, verifies zero references, marks ready to deleting and writes its outbox event transactionally before external deletion.
External deletion occurs outside PostgreSQL locks; logical/object usage is decremented and the attachment becomes deleted only after the required physical object versions are confirmed absent.
A delete marker alone or a failed VersionId deletion does not release usage, and a new reference to a deleting attachment receives ATTACHMENT_NOT_READY rather than reviving the object.
The same usage event/source/phase replay does not apply a second ledger delta.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic ledger and versioned-object inventory include reserved uploads, observed staging objects, a copying candidate, ready objects, an unreferenced ready attachment, and an unregistered provider object.
fixtures.action: Plan reconciliation after reserve expiry, copy/worker crash, provider timeout, quota decrease, and repeated pg-boss delivery.
assertions: Ledger byte and object counters remain nonnegative and account for reserved, staging, pending-final, and live objects until each corresponding physical cleanup is confirmed.
An expired reservation alone does not zero staging or candidate usage; an unknown copy result retains its reserved/pending accounting until reconciled.

A repeated worker event is idempotent by its source/phase key; unregistered objects enter only a restricted cleanup quarantine and are neither exposed to clients nor immediately released from accounting.
Storage failure or reduced entitlement blocks positive-delta uploads while reads, deletes, and export remain available; local saved data is not silently deleted.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic staging/candidate objects have signed URL and reservation timestamps around the configured 300-second upload URL and 600-second reservation lifetimes.
fixtures.action: Plan cleanup before URL expiry, after URL expiry, and after an uncertain provider delete; repeat HEAD/delete confirmation before reconciling usage.
assertions: Staging is not finally released before signed_until; deleting it earlier would permit an old still-valid conditional URL to recreate it.
URL expiry closes new signed writes/finalization as specified but does not by itself release staging/candidate accounting.
After expiry, cleanup rechecks physical versions and decrements usage only after deletion is confirmed; the plan does not infer provider semantics before T18's provider gate.

fixtures.setup: Construct synthetic backup manifests, entity snapshots, object-version inventories, post-backup delete records, device cursors, drafts, and ledgers in a disposable isolated recovery scenario. The stale backup carries deletion-watermark marker 25 while durable post-backup evidence carries marker 41; the marker encoding itself is not specified.
fixtures.action: Plan recovery while normal writes/downloads remain isolated; replay the stale backup marker 25, reconcile the external durable marker 41 and deletion records, then exercise complete-evidence and missing-evidence branches.
assertions: PostgreSQL and object backups are not presumed consistent; normal writes/downloads stay isolated until object/version and ledger reconciliation plus post-restore deletion checks are complete.
If deletion evidence cannot be proven complete, the recovered workspace remains isolated; backup presence alone is not a recovery pass.
Only after reconciliation and deletion-fence checks does the planned flow increase epoch and reopen clients through a fresh snapshot/bootstrap; old-epoch cursors cannot resume as current state.

A client recovers into a new namespace, catches up and validates before atomic swap; old unsent drafts and recovery copies stay local, and old draft/outbox data is not automatically uploaded around deletion fences.
Synthetic S25 isolation checks do not claim the production-equivalent operational rehearsal assigned to T29/T30.

With synthetic stale marker 25 and durable marker 41, recovered deletion watermark must not fall below 41 after backup replay; reapply post-backup deletions before reopening writes/downloads. The exact evidence source, completeness proof, and marker encoding remain OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: A synthetic snapshot build is in progress with no ready publication; request cancellation at controlled points before materialization commit and during a simulated worker interruption.
fixtures.action: Plan cancellation/worker-interruption probes against an isolated harness; do not assume a provider or successful backend result.
assertions: A canceled or interrupted build never exposes partial snapshot rows or pins as a ready snapshot; readiness is atomic with materialization.
Exact cancel acknowledgement, terminal job state, cleanup/retry timing, and cancellation race behavior remain OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: Create two synthetic workspaces and a principal authorized only for workspace A; seed distinguishable synthetic rows, snapshot rows/pins, and ledger entries in workspace B.
fixtures.action: Plan cross-workspace read and write attempts using B identifiers while each request is scoped to A.
assertions: Workspace B data and existence are not disclosed to the A-scoped principal; unauthorized business objects map to the specified RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND behavior.
No write, snapshot, pin, ledger, or object reference is created in workspace B by an A-scoped request.
No global hash lookup or worker scope bypass is used; the fixture asserts only the frozen isolation outcome.

fixtures.setup: Prepare a synthetic entity at maxVersionsPerEntity=20 with eligible and current/log/trash/snapshot-protected versions. Independently seed object counts live=199997, staging=1, pending-final=1, reserved=1, totaling maxStoredObjectsPerWorkspace=200000.
fixtures.action: Plan a new version at the version cap, an upload reserve requiring two object slots against the full object budget, the expired-but-unconfirmed cleanup candidate, and the eligible-version cleanup branch; model accounting only without calling an object-store provider.
assertions: An eligible unreferenced old version may be reclaimed only after all log, trash, snapshot, retention, and current-head protections clear; if the version cap remains full, reject the new version rather than silently deleting a protected version.
Stored-object accounting includes live, staging, pending-final, and reserved objects; an expired object remains counted until physical deletion is confirmed.

A reserve that would exceed the 200,000 stored-object cap is rejected before provider API work; live/staging/pending-final/reserved counters and usage ledger remain unchanged. The exact capacity code/details remain OPEN_QUESTION.

references: 03 §3.2 snapshots partial UNIQUE(wid) WHERE status IN (building,ready)
fixtures.setup: Use synthetic workspace A with one still-valid ready snapshot and workspace B with one building snapshot; keep the two workspaces independent.
fixtures.action: For A, request a snapshot while the ready snapshot remains valid. For B, issue a second snapshot request while the first remains building.
assertions: Each workspace has at most one snapshot in building or ready state at a time.
A request in workspace A reuses the existing still-valid ready snapshot identity rather than creating a duplicate active snapshot.
A second request in workspace B cannot create another building/ready snapshot while one is building; exact external response/job mapping for this request remains OPEN_QUESTION.

resourceGates.scope: Maximum legal snapshot dataset: 50,000 live entities including collection relationships, with retired IDs and old versions excluded from rowCount.
Maximum-row snapshot statement and workspace lock contention under the recorded isolated PostgreSQL plan.
Snapshot pin lifetime and end-to-end fixed paging, catchup through priorSeenHighWater, and bootstrap ACK within the 1,800-second TTL; measure elapsed time with a monotonic clock.
resourceGates.budget: cloud.snapshotTtlSeconds = 1,800 seconds; the complete page + catchup + bootstrap path must finish within TTL; monotonic elapsed-time gate is NOT_RUN; no paging connection/transaction is held between requests.

resourceGates.scope: Retired-ID, 20-version-per-entity, and 200,000 stored-object capacity boundaries, including protected-version and pending/reserved physical-object accounting.
S25 synthetic isolated recovery core and deletion-fence reconciliation.
resourceGates.budget: No numeric pass threshold beyond the frozen limits; missing deletion evidence keeps the workspace isolated.

blockedBy: corresponding recovery implementation and isolated test harness
corresponding snapshot/GC implementation and disposable PostgreSQL/object-store harness

openQuestions.topic: Exact snapshot over-row-limit, timeout, and failed-build externally visible result/worker terminal mapping; do not invent a code or retry policy.
Fixed hardware/PostgreSQL plan and the precise 2,000 ms experiment measurement boundary for the maximum-row snapshot; record actual plan and timing when the gate is authorized.

Exact worker cadence/retry and lease-expiry scheduling interface, plus any snapshot-TTL clock start boundary not stated by the accepted interface; frozen 90-day expiry and snapshot-required/bootstrap semantics are not open questions.

Exact external error/result mapping for a create rejected at the lifetime ID budget. The policy is frozen: reserve a retirement slot at create, never refuse delete, block further creates at the budget, offer export/explicit new-workspace migration, and never compact/delete fences.
Exact pg-boss job cancellation/retry/result mapping and cleanup semantics for a crash during building; only no-half-snapshot and frozen states are asserted.
T18 is not accepted: selected object-store provider/SDK exact immutable version, HEAD, conditional-delete, and delete-confirmation behavior remains a provider gate.
Durable post-backup deletion-evidence source/format and how its completeness is proved during disaster recovery are not defined; if unknown, remain isolated.
T16/T18 canonical worker, snapshot, ledger, and restore interfaces are not accepted; fixtures state only the already frozen externally observable semantics and add no DTO fields.
Exact endpoint-to-code/details allocation within the frozen 507 capacity error family for a still-full protected-version or stored-object boundary; do not invent a mapping.

limitations: This is a synthetic fixture/interface plan only; no fixture behavior, benchmark, PostgreSQL operation, object-store call, package command, build, or service was executed.
T16 and T18 are not accepted, so production behavior and provider equivalence cannot be inferred from these fixtures.
All 2-second/50,000-row, TTL, lease, ledger, and recovery gates remain NOT_RUN; configured planning budgets are not performance results.
Production-equivalent disaster-recovery rehearsal and account-delete UI remain assigned to T29/T30.
